item.title: The Detective's Maxim: A Victorian Cryptogram
item.description:
You spot a two-letter word that starts with the free T. It has to be TO. You fill in the O, and suddenly an eight-letter word reads T _ _ O _ _ _ _ and your brain refuses to let it go. Five minutes later you’re muttering at a 135-year-old sentence about evidence. That’s the cryptogram effect: one right guess pays for itself everywhere the letter appears.

Every letter in the quote below has been swapped for a different letter, and the swap holds for the whole puzzle. If K means E once, it means E every time. No letter ever stands for itself. You get one letter free.
